decisions.reason: As a low-cost plugin close to the core webshop optimization business, it still has option value and there is no clear negative evidence yet to justify withdrawal after only one year.
An ERP interface plugin fits the firm's move toward broader multichannel commerce support and is strategically complementary, so management would likely keep this option open.
Although another price-comparison tracking plugin faces some portfolio overlap, it is still near the established offer and likely inexpensive to maintain, so it would usually be retained for now.
Given the growing e-commerce market and the limited downside of keeping a close-to-core plugin on offer, management would probably continue this product despite some redundancy risk.
This plugin remains a plausible option on a growing platform-services base, and without stronger evidence of weak demand the firm would be inclined to wait rather than abandon it.

A net price reporting plugin is adjacent to the firm's existing technical and analytics capabilities, so the expected cost of keeping it is likely low relative to the value of learning more about demand.
